title: Unknown probability mass and unknown observability are different
problem: Extend R37's known-class audit model to an unclassified defect region without pretending its detection sensitivity is known.
failure: A label UNKNOWN does not supply a detection mechanism. If zero sensitivity is admissible, repeating tests cannot remove the worst-case unknown mass. Indistinguishable observable transcript distributions cannot identify distinct worlds.
correction: Separate prior mass from detection capability. For a two-region model with known conditional miss rates and uncertain prior interval, worst miss is the maximum at the interval endpoints; discrete convexity permits exact deterministic allocation by binary search. Use independent challenge evidence for sensitivity bounds.
transfer: Reserve exploration for mechanisms outside the current classification and state the coverage assumptions. Do not infer that no unknown defects exist from all-negative tests. Distinguish anomaly detection from explanation.
limits: Single persistent defect, two disjoint regions, equal cost, conditional independent detection, fixed horizon. 4875 allocation cases, 34125 exact comparisons, 51 zero-sensitivity checks, 1022 finite subset checks. Randomized allocation minimax not analyzed. No empirical sensitivity calibration, production, novelty or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
